_comment: Kid-level English for each verse, keyed "<chapter>:<verse>". Written by hand at P2/P3 reading level: what the verse is saying, not a formal translation. Read by scripts/build_bible_text.py.
1:1: The wise sayings of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel.
1:2: They help you learn to be wise, and to understand what people mean.
1:3: They teach you to live well: to be kind, to be fair, and to be honest.
1:4: They make a simple person clever, and give a young person knowledge and good sense.
1:5: A wise person listens and learns even more; a clever person learns how to decide well.
1:6: They help you understand wise sayings, word pictures, and riddles.
1:7: Respecting the LORD is where knowledge begins. Only fools look down on wisdom and teaching.
1:8: My son, listen to your father's teaching, and do not turn away from your mother's rules.
1:9: They will be like a beautiful crown on your head and a chain around your neck.
1:10: My son, if bad people try to tempt you, do not go along with them.
1:11: They may say: Come with us! Let's hide and wait, and hurt someone who has done nothing wrong.
1:12: They say: We will swallow them up alive, like a deep pit swallowing people whole.
1:13: They say: We will get all kinds of treasure and fill our houses with what we take.
1:14: They say: Join us! We will all share one money bag together.
1:15: My son, do not walk down that road with them. Keep your feet away from their path.
1:16: Their feet run to do wrong, and they hurry to hurt other people.
1:17: It is no use setting a net where the bird can see it.
1:18: But these people are really hiding to hurt themselves; they are trapping their own lives.
1:19: That is what happens to everyone who is greedy for money: greed takes away their own life.
1:20: Wisdom calls out loudly in the street, and raises her voice in the open square.
1:21: She shouts at the busy corner, at the city gate, and all through the town.
1:22: She says: You simple people, how long will you love being foolish? How long will you laugh at what is good and hate knowing things?
1:23: Turn around and listen when I correct you! Then I will pour out my spirit on you and tell you what I think.
1:24: I called, but you would not listen. I reached out my hand, but nobody paid attention.
1:25: You ignored all my advice and would not take my correction.
1:26: So when trouble comes, I will laugh; when you are afraid, I will not feel sorry for you.
1:27: Fear will come at you like a strong wind, and trouble like a storm; pain and worry will come upon you.
1:28: Then you will call me, but I will not answer; you will look everywhere for me, but you will not find me.
1:29: That is because you hated knowing things, and did not want to respect the LORD.
1:30: You would not take my advice, and you looked down on every correction I gave.
1:31: So you will eat the fruit of what you planted, and get your fill of your own plans.
1:32: Simple people are killed by turning away, and fools are destroyed by not caring.
1:33: But whoever listens to me will live safely, and rest quietly with nothing to fear.
2:1: My son, if you take in what I say and keep my commands safe,
2:2: listening carefully to wisdom and setting your heart on understanding;
2:3: yes, if you call out for good sense and ask loudly for understanding,
2:4: if you look for it like silver and search for it like hidden treasure,
2:5: then you will understand what it means to respect the LORD, and you will come to know God.
2:6: It is the LORD who gives wisdom; knowledge and understanding come out of his mouth.
2:7: He saves up real wisdom for those who do right; he is a shield for people who live honestly.
2:8: He guards the paths of fair people and watches over the way of those who love him.
2:9: Then you will understand what is right, what is fair, what is honest — every good path.
2:10: Wisdom will come into your heart, and knowing things will make you glad.
2:11: Good sense will watch over you, and understanding will keep you safe.
2:12: It will save you from the wrong road, and from people who twist their words.
2:13: Those people leave the straight path and walk in dark ways.
2:14: They are happy doing wrong, and they enjoy how twisted bad people are.
2:15: Their ways are crooked, and their paths wander off.
2:16: Wisdom will save you from a woman who is not your wife, whose smooth words are meant to trick you.
2:17: She left the husband of her young days and forgot the promise she made before God.
2:18: Her house leads down to death, and her path leads to the place of the dead.
2:19: Nobody who goes to her comes back, or finds the road to life again.
2:20: So wisdom will keep you walking the way of good people and on the path of those who do right.
2:21: Honest people will live in the land, and those who are whole-hearted will stay in it.
2:22: But bad people will be cut off from the land, and cheats will be pulled up by the roots.
3:1: My son, do not forget what I teach you; let your heart keep my commands,
3:2: because they will add to your life many days, long years, and peace.
3:3: Never let kindness and honesty leave you. Tie them around your neck; write them on your heart.
3:4: Then God and people will think well of you, and you will have good sense.
3:5: Trust the LORD with your whole heart, and do not lean on how clever you think you are.
3:6: Remember him in everything you do, and he will make your paths straight.
3:7: Do not think you are wise all by yourself. Respect the LORD and stay away from what is wrong.
3:8: That will be good health for your body and strength deep in your bones.
3:9: Honour the LORD with what you own, and with the first and best of everything you grow.
3:10: Then your storerooms will be full, and your barrels will overflow with new wine.
3:11: My son, do not brush off the LORD's teaching, and do not get tired of being corrected,
3:12: because the LORD corrects the ones he loves, just like a father corrects the son he is proud of.
3:13: How happy is the person who finds wisdom and gets understanding!
3:14: Having wisdom is better than having silver, and worth more than pure gold.
3:15: She is more precious than jewels, and nothing you could wish for compares with her.
3:16: In her right hand is a long life; in her left hand are riches and honour.
3:17: Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths are peaceful.
3:18: She is a tree of life to everyone who holds on to her; whoever keeps her is happy.
3:19: By wisdom the LORD made the earth; by understanding he set the sky in place.
3:20: By what he knows, the deep waters opened up and the clouds drop down dew.
3:21: My son, hold on to real wisdom and good sense; do not let them out of your sight.
3:22: They will be life to you, and something beautiful around your neck.
3:23: Then you will walk your road safely, and your foot will not trip.
3:24: When you lie down you will not be afraid; you will lie down and sleep sweetly.
3:25: Do not be frightened when something scary happens suddenly, or when trouble hits bad people,
3:26: because the LORD is the one you trust, and he will keep your foot out of the trap.
3:27: If you have the power to help someone, do not hold it back from the person who needs it.
3:28: Do not say to your neighbour, "Go away, come back tomorrow and I'll give it" — when you have it right now.
3:29: Do not plan to hurt your neighbour, who lives beside you trusting you.
3:30: Do not pick a fight with someone for no reason, when they have done you no harm.
3:31: Do not be jealous of a bully, or choose to copy any of his ways,
3:32: because the LORD hates a twisted person, but he is close friends with those who do right.
3:33: The LORD's curse is on the home of bad people, but he blesses the home of those who do right.
3:34: He laughs at people who sneer, but he is kind to people who are humble.
3:35: Wise people will be given honour, but fools get shame even when they rise up.
4:1: Children, listen to a father's teaching, and pay attention so you can understand.
4:2: What I am giving you is good teaching; do not turn away from it.
4:3: I too was a son to my father, and in my mother's eyes her only precious boy.
4:4: He taught me and said: hold my words in your heart; keep my commands and you will live.
4:5: Get wisdom, get understanding. Do not forget, and do not turn away from what I say.
4:6: Do not leave wisdom behind, and she will protect you; love her, and she will keep you safe.
4:7: Wisdom is the most important thing, so get wisdom. Whatever else you get, get understanding.
4:8: Treasure her, and she will lift you up; hold her close, and she will bring you honour.
4:9: She will put a beautiful crown on your head and hand you a crown of glory.
4:10: My son, listen and take in what I say, and the years of your life will be many.
4:11: I have taught you the way of wisdom and led you along straight paths.
4:12: When you walk, your steps will not be blocked; when you run, you will not trip.
4:13: Hold tight to what you have been taught. Do not let go — it is your life.
4:14: Do not go down the road of bad people, or walk the way of those who do wrong.
4:15: Stay away from it, do not pass by it; turn around and go.
4:16: Those people cannot sleep unless they have done something wrong; they lie awake unless they have made someone fall.
4:17: Doing wrong is like bread to them, and being cruel is like wine.
4:18: But the path of people who do right is like the morning light, getting brighter and brighter until noon.
4:19: The way of bad people is like the dark; they do not even know what they tripped over.
4:20: My son, pay attention to what I say; listen carefully to my words.
4:21: Do not let them out of your sight; keep them deep in your heart,
4:22: because they are life to whoever finds them, and healing for the whole body.
4:23: Guard your heart more than anything else, because everything you do flows out of it.
4:24: Get rid of crooked talk; keep twisted words far away from you.
4:25: Let your eyes look straight ahead; keep your gaze fixed in front of you.
4:26: Think carefully about the path your feet are on, and all your ways will be steady.
4:27: Do not turn off to the right or the left; keep your foot away from what is wrong.
5:1: My son, pay attention to my wise words; listen carefully to what I understand.
5:2: Then you will keep good sense, and your lips will hold on to what you know.
5:3: The lips of a woman who is not your wife drip honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil,
5:4: but in the end she is bitter as poison and sharp as a two-edged sword.
5:5: Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to the place of the dead.
5:6: She never thinks about the road to life; her paths wander, and she does not even know it.
5:7: So now, children, listen to me, and do not turn away from what I say.
5:8: Keep far away from her; do not even go near the door of her house,
5:9: or you will give your good name to others and your best years to someone cruel,
5:10: and strangers will be filled with what you worked for, and your hard work will end up in someone else's house.
5:11: At the end you will groan, when your body and your health are worn away,
5:12: and you will say: how I hated being taught! How my heart pushed away correction!
5:13: I did not listen to my teachers, or pay attention to the people who taught me.
5:14: I was nearly ruined completely, right in front of everybody.
5:15: Drink water from your own well, running water from your own spring.
5:16: Why should your springs spill out into the street for anyone at all?
5:17: Let them be yours alone, and not shared with strangers.
5:18: May your spring be blessed, and may you be happy with the wife you married when you were young.
5:19: She is like a graceful deer; let her love make you glad and content always.
5:20: My son, why would you go after a woman who is not your wife?
5:21: Everything a person does is right in front of the LORD's eyes; he sees all their paths.
5:22: A bad person gets caught by his own wrongdoing; his own sins tie him up like ropes.
5:23: He dies because he would not be taught, and his great foolishness leads him off the road.
6:1: My son, if you have promised to pay a friend's debt, or shaken hands on a stranger's loan,
6:2: then you are caught by your own words, trapped by what your own mouth said.
6:3: So do this, my son, and get yourself free: you are in your friend's hands, so go, humble yourself, and beg him to let you off.
6:4: Do not let your eyes sleep, or your eyelids close.
6:5: Get free like a deer escaping the hunter, like a bird escaping the bird-catcher.
6:6: You lazy person, go and watch an ant. Look at what it does, and learn to be wise.
6:7: An ant has no leader, no boss, and no king,
6:8: yet it stores up its food in summer and gathers its meals at harvest time.
6:9: You lazy person, how long will you lie there? When will you get up from your sleep?
6:10: A little more sleep, a little more dozing, a little more folding your hands to rest —
6:11: and being poor will come at you like a robber, and going without like an armed man.
6:12: A good-for-nothing troublemaker goes around with a crooked mouth.
6:13: He winks his eyes, shuffles his feet, and points his fingers to signal others.
6:14: His heart is twisted; he is always planning trouble and starting fights.
6:15: So disaster will hit him suddenly; in a moment he will be broken, past mending.
6:16: There are six things the LORD hates, seven that he cannot stand:
6:17: proud eyes, a lying tongue, hands that hurt innocent people,
6:18: a heart that plans wicked things, feet that run quickly to do wrong,
6:19: a false witness who tells lies, and anyone who stirs up fights between brothers.
6:20: My son, keep your father's command, and do not turn away from your mother's teaching.
6:21: Tie them onto your heart always; hang them around your neck.
6:22: When you walk, they will lead you; when you sleep, they will watch over you; when you wake, they will talk with you.
6:23: A command is a lamp, teaching is a light, and being corrected is the road to life.
6:24: They will keep you away from a bad woman and from her smooth, flattering words.
6:25: Do not long for her beauty in your heart, or let her looks catch you.
6:26: Chasing that kind of woman can cost you everything you have, and even your life.
6:27: Can a man scoop fire into his shirt without burning his clothes?
6:28: Can someone walk on hot coals without burning his feet?
6:29: It is the same for anyone who goes after his neighbour's wife: nobody who touches her gets off free.
6:30: People do not look down on a thief who steals because he is starving,
6:31: but if he is caught, he must pay back seven times, even everything in his house.
6:32: Anyone who breaks a marriage has no sense at all; he destroys his own life doing it.
6:33: He will get wounds and shame, and the disgrace will never be wiped away,
6:34: because a jealous husband becomes furious, and he will show no mercy when he takes revenge.
6:35: He will not accept any payment, and no amount of gifts will calm him down.
7:1: My son, keep my words and store up my commands inside you.
7:2: Keep my commands and you will live; guard my teaching like the pupil of your eye.
7:3: Tie them onto your fingers; write them on your heart.
7:4: Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding your close relative.
7:5: They will keep you away from a woman who is not your wife, and from her flattering words.
7:6: From the window of my house I looked out through the lattice,
7:7: and among the simple young people I noticed one young man with no sense at all.
7:8: He went down the street near her corner, walking straight towards her house,
7:9: in the twilight, in the evening, in the dark of the night.
7:10: And look — a woman came out to meet him, dressed to attract him, with a sly heart.
7:11: She is loud and will not be told anything; she never stays home.
7:12: Sometimes in the street, sometimes in the square, waiting at every corner.
7:13: She grabbed the young man and kissed him, and with a bold face she said to him:
7:14: "I had an offering to make, and today I finished what I promised.
7:15: That is why I came out to meet you; I was looking for you, and here you are!
7:16: I have covered my bed with pretty blankets and fine cloth from Egypt.
7:17: I have made my bed smell sweet with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
7:18: Come, let's enjoy ourselves until morning; let's be happy together.
7:19: My husband is not home; he has gone on a long journey.
7:20: He took a bag of money with him and will not be back until the full moon."
7:21: With all her smooth talking she won him over; her flattering lips pulled him along.
7:22: He followed her at once, like an ox walking to be killed, like a fool going to be punished,
7:23: until an arrow goes through him — like a bird rushing into a net, not knowing it will cost his life.
7:24: So now, children, listen to me; pay attention to what I say.
7:25: Do not let your heart turn down her road; do not wander onto her paths,
7:26: because she has knocked down so many, and even strong people have been destroyed by her.
7:27: Her house is the road to the place of the dead, going down to the rooms of death.
8:1: Listen — is wisdom not calling out? Is understanding not raising her voice?
8:2: She stands on the high places beside the road, where the paths meet.
8:3: Beside the gates, at the entrance to the city, at the doorways, she calls out loudly:
8:4: "I am calling to all of you, everybody; I am speaking to every person.
8:5: You who are simple, learn some sense; you who are foolish, understand in your heart.
8:6: Listen, because I will say excellent things; what I open my mouth to say is right.
8:7: My mouth speaks the truth, and my lips hate what is wrong.
8:8: Everything I say is fair; nothing in it is twisted or crooked.
8:9: It is all clear to a person who understands, and right to anyone who has found knowledge.
8:10: Take my teaching instead of silver, and knowledge instead of the finest gold,
8:11: because wisdom is better than jewels, and nothing you could want compares with her.
8:12: I, wisdom, live together with good sense, and I know how to plan well.
8:13: Respecting the LORD means hating what is evil. I hate pride, showing off, the wrong road, and a twisted mouth.
8:14: Good advice and real wisdom are mine; I am understanding, and I have strength.
8:15: Kings rule because of me, and leaders make fair decisions.
8:16: Princes and nobles and every fair judge on earth govern through me.
8:17: I love those who love me, and whoever looks for me carefully will find me.
8:18: Riches and honour are with me, lasting wealth and doing what is right.
8:19: What I give is better than gold, even pure gold, and better than the finest silver.
8:20: I walk along the road of doing right, on the paths of fairness,
8:21: giving real riches to those who love me, and filling up their storerooms.
8:22: The LORD had me at the very beginning, before he made anything else.
8:23: I was set in place long, long ago, before the world began.
8:24: Before there were any deep seas, before there were any springs of water, I was born.
8:25: Before the mountains were set in place, before the hills, I was born.
8:26: This was before he made the earth, or the fields, or the first speck of dust in the world.
8:27: When he put the sky in place, I was there; when he drew a circle around the deep sea,
8:28: when he set the clouds above and made the springs of the deep strong,
8:29: when he told the sea how far it could come and laid the foundations of the earth —
8:30: I was beside him like a master builder. I was his delight day after day, always glad in front of him,
8:31: glad about the world he made, and happy to be with people.
8:32: So now, children, listen to me: happy are those who keep to my ways.
8:33: Listen to teaching and be wise; do not throw it away.
8:34: Happy is the person who listens to me, waiting at my door every day, watching beside my gate,
8:35: because whoever finds me finds life, and the LORD will be pleased with them.
8:36: But whoever misses me hurts their own self; everyone who hates me loves death."
9:1: Wisdom has built her house and carved out its seven pillars.
9:2: She has prepared her meat, mixed her wine, and set her table.
9:3: She has sent out her servant girls, and she calls from the highest places in the city:
9:4: "Whoever is simple, come in here!" And to anyone with no sense she says,
9:5: "Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
9:6: Leave foolish ways behind and you will live; walk on the road of understanding."
9:7: Correct someone who sneers and you will only get insulted; correct a bad person and you will get hurt.
9:8: Do not correct a person who sneers, or he will hate you. Correct a wise person, and he will love you.
9:9: Teach a wise person and he becomes wiser still; teach a good person and he learns even more.
9:10: Respecting the LORD is where wisdom begins, and knowing the Holy One is understanding.
9:11: Through me your days will be many, and years will be added to your life.
9:12: If you are wise, it is good for you; if you sneer at everything, you carry that by yourself.
9:13: A foolish woman is loud; she is simple and knows nothing at all.
9:14: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high part of the city,
9:15: calling out to people going past, who are going straight on their way:
9:16: "Whoever is simple, come in here!" And to anyone with no sense she says,
9:17: "Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret tastes good."
9:18: But he does not know that the dead are there, and that her guests are deep in the place of the dead.
10:1: The wise sayings of Solomon. A wise son makes his father glad; a foolish son makes his mother sad.
10:2: Money got by doing wrong is no use at all, but doing right saves a person from death.
10:3: The LORD will not let a good person go hungry, but he pushes away what bad people are greedy for.
10:4: Lazy hands make a person poor, but hard-working hands make a person rich.
10:5: Gathering crops in summer is what a wise son does; sleeping through harvest is what a shameful son does.
10:6: Blessings rest on the head of a good person, but violence covers the mouth of a bad one.
10:7: People remember a good person kindly, but the name of a bad person rots away.
10:8: A wise heart takes in commands, but a person who babbles foolishly will fall.
10:9: Walking honestly means walking safely; walking crooked ways means being found out.
10:10: Someone who winks slyly causes trouble, and a person who babbles foolishly will fall.
10:11: A good person's mouth is a well of life, but violence covers the mouth of a bad one.
10:12: Hate stirs up quarrels, but love covers over every wrong.
10:13: Wisdom is found on the lips of someone who understands, but a stick is for the back of someone with no sense.
10:14: Wise people store up what they know, but a fool's mouth brings ruin close.
10:15: A rich person's money is like a strong city; being poor is what ruins the poor.
10:16: A good person's work leads to life; what a bad person earns leads to sin.
10:17: Whoever keeps to teaching is on the road of life, but whoever refuses correction gets lost.
10:18: Hiding hate means lying lips, and spreading gossip makes a person a fool.
10:19: Too many words always bring wrongdoing; holding your tongue is wise.
10:20: A good person's tongue is like fine silver; a bad person's heart is worth very little.
10:21: A good person's words feed many, but fools die because they have no sense.
10:22: The LORD's blessing makes a person rich, and he adds no sorrow to it.
10:23: A fool thinks doing wrong is a game, but a person who understands enjoys wisdom.
10:24: What a bad person dreads will happen to them; what a good person wants will be given.
10:25: When the storm passes, bad people are gone, but good people stand firm for ever.
10:26: Like vinegar on the teeth or smoke in the eyes, that is what a lazy person is to whoever sends him.
10:27: Respecting the LORD adds days to your life, but a bad person's years are cut short.
10:28: What good people hope for ends in joy, but what bad people expect comes to nothing.
10:29: The LORD's way is a safe place for honest people, but ruin for those who do wrong.
10:30: Good people will never be shaken loose, but bad people will not stay in the land.
10:31: A good person's mouth grows wisdom, but a twisted tongue will be cut off.
10:32: A good person's lips know what is fitting, but a bad person's mouth says twisted things.
11:1: The LORD hates a scale that cheats, but an honest weight makes him glad.
11:2: When pride comes, shame comes with it, but humble people have wisdom.
11:3: Honest people are guided by being honest, but cheats are destroyed by their own crookedness.
11:4: Money is no help on the day of anger, but doing right saves a person from death.
11:5: Doing right makes a whole-hearted person's path straight, but bad people fall over their own badness.
11:6: Honest people are rescued by doing right, but cheats are trapped by their own greed.
11:7: When a bad person dies, everything they expected dies too; all they hoped for comes to nothing.
11:8: A good person is brought safely out of trouble, and the bad person ends up there instead.
11:9: A person who pretends can ruin a neighbour with their mouth, but knowing things rescues good people.
11:10: When good people do well, the whole city is glad; when bad people fall, people shout for joy.
11:11: A city is lifted up by the blessing of honest people, but pulled down by the mouths of bad ones.
11:12: Looking down on your neighbour shows no sense; someone who understands keeps quiet.
11:13: A gossip gives away secrets, but someone trustworthy keeps a matter hidden.
11:14: Without good advice a people falls, but with many advisers there is safety.
11:15: Promising to pay a stranger's debt brings loss, but refusing to shake on it keeps you safe.
11:16: A kind woman is honoured, and forceful men get rich.
11:17: A kind person does themselves good, but a cruel person brings trouble on themselves.
11:18: A bad person earns empty wages, but whoever plants what is right gets a real reward.
11:19: Sticking to what is right leads to life; chasing what is evil leads to death.
11:20: The LORD hates a twisted heart, but he delights in people who live whole and straight.
11:21: Be sure of this: bad people will not go unpunished, but the children of good people will be safe.
11:22: A beautiful woman with no sense is like a gold ring in a pig's nose.
11:23: What good people want ends in good; what bad people expect ends in anger.
11:24: One person gives freely and gets more; another holds back too much and ends up poor.
11:25: A generous person will do well; whoever gives others a drink will be given one.
11:26: People curse whoever hoards grain, but they bless whoever is willing to sell it.
11:27: Whoever works hard at doing good finds kindness, but whoever looks for trouble will get it.
11:28: Whoever leans on their money will fall, but good people grow green like a leaf.
11:29: Whoever brings trouble on their own family inherits nothing but wind, and a fool ends up serving the wise.
11:30: What a good person grows is a tree of life, and a wise person wins others over.
11:31: Look — if good people get what is coming to them here on earth, how much more bad people and sinners!
12:1: Loving to be taught means loving to learn; hating correction is like being an animal.
12:2: A good person is shown kindness by the LORD, but he judges anyone who makes sly plans.
12:3: Nobody stands firm by doing wrong, but a good person's roots will never be moved.
12:4: A capable wife is her husband's crown, but a shameful one is like rot in his bones.
12:5: Good people think about what is fair; bad people's plans are full of tricks.
12:6: Bad people's words lie in wait to hurt others, but honest people's words rescue them.
12:7: Bad people are knocked over and gone, but a good person's house keeps standing.
12:8: A person is praised for how wise they are, but a twisted heart is looked down on.
12:9: Better to be nobody special and have a servant than to act important and have no food.
12:10: A good person cares about their animals, but even the kindness of bad people is cruel.
12:11: Whoever works their own field will have plenty to eat, but chasing empty things shows no sense.
12:12: Bad people want what other bad people have caught, but a good person's roots produce fruit.
12:13: A bad person is trapped by their own sinful talk, but a good person gets out of trouble.
12:14: What a person says fills them with good things, and what their hands do comes back to them.
12:15: A fool thinks his own way is right, but a wise person listens to advice.
12:16: A fool shows his anger straight away, but a sensible person lets an insult pass.
12:17: Telling the truth shows what is right; a false witness shows nothing but tricks.
12:18: Careless words stab like a sword, but the tongue of a wise person heals.
12:19: True words last for ever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
12:20: Those who plan evil have tricks in their hearts, but those who work for peace have joy.
12:21: No real harm comes to a good person, but bad people are filled with trouble.
12:22: The LORD hates lying lips, but he delights in people who act honestly.
12:23: A sensible person keeps what they know to themselves, but a foolish heart shouts out its foolishness.
12:24: Hard-working hands will end up in charge, but lazy ones will end up doing forced work.
12:25: Worry weighs a person's heart down, but one kind word makes it glad.
12:26: A good person guides their neighbour, but the way of bad people leads others astray.
12:27: A lazy person does not even cook what he caught, but a hard-working person treasures what he has.
12:28: On the road of doing right there is life, and along that path there is no death.
13:1: A wise son listens to his father's teaching, but someone who sneers will not listen to correction.
13:2: A person enjoys good things from what they say, but cheats hunger for violence.
13:3: Guarding your mouth guards your life; opening it wide brings ruin.
13:4: A lazy person wants things but gets nothing; a hard-working person gets plenty.
13:5: A good person hates lying; a bad person earns a bad name and ends up ashamed.
13:6: Doing right keeps an honest person safe, but doing wrong knocks a sinner over.
13:7: One person pretends to be rich and has nothing; another pretends to be poor and has plenty.
13:8: A rich person may have to pay to save their life, but a poor person never even hears the threat.
13:9: A good person's light shines brightly, but a bad person's lamp goes out.
13:10: Pride only starts arguments, but those who take advice are wise.
13:11: Money that comes too easily disappears, but saving little by little makes it grow.
13:12: Hoping for something that never comes makes the heart sick, but getting what you longed for is a tree of life.
13:13: Whoever laughs at good teaching brings ruin on themselves, but whoever respects a command is rewarded.
13:14: A wise person's teaching is a fountain of life that turns you away from deadly traps.
13:15: Good sense wins people over, but the road of cheats is rough going.
13:16: A sensible person acts on what they know, but a fool spreads his foolishness around.
13:17: A bad messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy one brings healing.
13:18: Refusing to be taught brings poverty and shame, but taking correction brings honour.
13:19: Getting what you longed for is sweet, but fools hate to turn away from what is wrong.
13:20: Walk with wise people and you will be wise; keep company with fools and you will suffer.
13:21: Trouble chases sinners, but good people are paid back with good.
13:22: A good person leaves something behind for their grandchildren, but a sinner's wealth ends up with the good.
13:23: A poor person's field can grow plenty of food, but unfairness sweeps it away.
13:24: Whoever never corrects his son does not really love him; whoever loves him corrects him in good time.
13:25: A good person eats until they are full, but a bad person's stomach goes empty.
14:1: A wise woman builds up her home, but a foolish one pulls it down with her own hands.
14:2: Living honestly shows you respect the LORD; living crookedly shows you look down on him.
14:3: A fool's proud talk is a stick on his own back, but wise lips keep a person safe.
14:4: With no ox the feeding trough stays clean, but it takes an ox's strength to bring in a big harvest.
14:5: A truthful witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
14:6: Someone who sneers looks for wisdom and never finds it, but knowledge comes easily to a person who understands.
14:7: Walk away from a foolish person; you will find no knowledge on his lips.
14:8: A sensible person's wisdom is understanding their own way; a fool's foolishness is fooling themselves.
14:9: Fools laugh at doing wrong, but good people treat each other kindly.
14:10: Your heart knows its own sadness, and a stranger cannot share its joy.
14:11: The house of bad people will be knocked down, but the tent of honest people will do well.
14:12: There is a road that looks right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
14:13: Even while laughing the heart can ache, and that happiness can end in sadness.
14:14: A person whose heart turns away gets filled with their own ways, but a good person is satisfied with theirs.
14:15: A simple person believes anything, but a sensible person watches every step.
14:16: A wise person is careful and stays away from wrong, but a fool rages and is sure of himself.
14:17: Getting angry quickly makes a person act foolishly, and someone full of sly plans is hated.
14:18: Simple people end up with foolishness, but sensible people are crowned with knowledge.
14:19: Bad people will bow down before good people, and the wicked at the gate of those who do right.
14:20: A poor person is disliked even by their neighbour, but a rich person has many friends.
14:21: Looking down on your neighbour is doing wrong, but being kind to poor people brings happiness.
14:22: Do those who plan evil not go astray? But those who plan good find kindness and honesty.
14:23: All hard work brings something in, but talk alone leads to being poor.
14:24: Wise people's riches are their crown, but the foolishness of fools stays foolishness.
14:25: A truthful witness saves lives, but someone who pours out lies is playing tricks.
14:26: Respecting the LORD makes a person strong and sure, and gives their children a safe place.
14:27: Respecting the LORD is a fountain of life that turns you away from deadly traps.
14:28: A king's glory is having many people; a ruler is ruined when there are few.
14:29: Being slow to get angry shows real understanding; a quick temper shows great foolishness.
14:30: A peaceful heart gives the body life, but jealousy rots the bones.
14:31: Bullying a poor person insults the God who made them, but being kind to the needy honours him.
14:32: Bad people are knocked down by their own wrongdoing, but a good person has somewhere to turn even in death.
14:33: Wisdom rests in the heart of a person who understands, but what is in a fool's heart shows plainly.
14:34: Doing right lifts a nation up, but doing wrong brings shame on a people.
14:35: A king is pleased with a wise servant, but angry with one who brings shame.
15:1: A gentle answer calms anger down, but harsh words stir it up.
15:2: A wise person's tongue uses knowledge well, but a fool's mouth pours out foolishness.
15:3: The LORD's eyes are everywhere, watching both the bad and the good.
15:4: A kind tongue is a tree of life, but a twisted one breaks a person's spirit.
15:5: A fool looks down on his father's teaching, but taking correction makes a person sensible.
15:6: A good person's house holds much treasure, but what a bad person earns brings trouble.
15:7: Wise lips spread knowledge around; a foolish heart does nothing of the kind.
15:8: The LORD hates what a bad person offers, but the prayer of an honest person makes him glad.
15:9: The LORD hates the road bad people walk, but he loves whoever chases after what is right.
15:10: Leaving the right path brings hard correction, and hating correction leads to death.
15:11: Even the place of the dead lies open before the LORD — how much more a person's heart!
15:12: Someone who sneers does not like being corrected, and will not go near wise people.
15:13: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but a sad heart crushes the spirit.
15:14: A person who understands looks for knowledge, but a fool's mouth feeds on foolishness.
15:15: Every day is hard for someone who is suffering, but a cheerful heart is like a feast that never ends.
15:16: Better to have little and respect the LORD than to have great treasure and live in turmoil.
15:17: Better a dinner of vegetables where there is love than a fat roast where there is hate.
15:18: A hot-tempered person stirs up quarrels, but someone slow to anger calms them down.
15:19: A lazy person's road is like a hedge of thorns, but an honest person's path is a level highway.
15:20: A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish person looks down on his mother.
15:21: Foolishness is fun to someone with no sense, but a person who understands walks straight.
15:22: Without talking it over, plans fall apart; with many advisers, they succeed.
15:23: It is a joy to give a good answer, and a word at just the right time — how good that is!
15:24: For a wise person the road of life leads upward, away from the place of the dead below.
15:25: The LORD tears down a proud person's house, but he protects a widow's boundary line.
15:26: The LORD hates wicked plans, but kind words are pure to him.
15:27: Being greedy for money brings trouble on your own family, but hating bribes brings life.
15:28: A good person thinks before answering, but a bad person's mouth pours out evil.
15:29: The LORD stays far from bad people, but he listens to the prayer of good ones.
15:30: A bright look makes the heart glad, and good news gives strength to the bones.
15:31: Whoever listens to correction that gives life will be at home among the wise.
15:32: Refusing to be taught means not caring about your own life; taking correction means gaining sense.
15:33: Respecting the LORD teaches you wisdom, and humility comes before honour.
16:1: People plan things in their hearts, but the right answer on the tongue comes from the LORD.
16:2: Everything a person does looks clean to them, but the LORD weighs what is really inside.
16:3: Hand over what you do to the LORD, and your plans will stand firm.
16:4: The LORD made everything for its own purpose, even bad people for the day of trouble.
16:5: The LORD hates every proud heart. Be sure of this: such a person will not go unpunished.
16:6: Kindness and honesty make up for wrongdoing, and respecting the LORD keeps a person away from evil.
16:7: When the LORD is pleased with how a person lives, he makes even their enemies live at peace with them.
16:8: Better to have a little and be fair than to have plenty by being unfair.
16:9: A person plans their own road, but the LORD is the one who guides their steps.
16:10: A king's lips speak with authority; his mouth should not go wrong when he judges.
16:11: Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are his doing.
16:12: Kings should hate doing wrong, because a throne stands firm on doing right.
16:13: Kings are pleased with honest lips, and they love whoever speaks the truth.
16:14: A king's anger is like a messenger of death, but a wise person can calm it down.
16:15: When a king's face lights up, there is life; his kindness is like a rain cloud in spring.
16:16: Getting wisdom is far better than getting gold, and understanding is better to choose than silver.
16:17: The highway of honest people leads away from evil; guarding your path guards your life.
16:18: Pride comes before a crash, and a proud spirit before a fall.
16:19: Better to be humble among poor people than to share stolen goods with proud ones.
16:20: Whoever pays attention to teaching will do well, and whoever trusts the LORD is happy.
16:21: A wise heart is called sensible, and kind words help people learn more.
16:22: Understanding is a fountain of life to whoever has it, but foolishness is its own punishment.
16:23: A wise heart teaches the mouth what to say and helps the lips teach others.
16:24: Kind words are like a honeycomb: sweet to the heart and healing to the bones.
16:25: There is a road that looks right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
16:26: A worker's hunger keeps him working, because his empty stomach keeps pushing him on.
16:27: A worthless person digs up trouble, and his talk is like a burning fire.
16:28: A twisted person starts fights, and a gossip splits close friends apart.
16:29: A violent person tempts his neighbour and leads him down a road that is not good.
16:30: Someone who narrows his eyes is planning something twisted; someone who tightens his lips is set on evil.
16:31: Grey hair is a crown of glory, won by living the right way.
16:32: Being slow to anger is better than being a great soldier, and ruling your own heart is better than capturing a city.
16:33: The lot is thrown into the lap, but every decision comes from the LORD.
17:1: Better a dry crust with peace and quiet than a house full of feasting with fighting.
17:2: A clever servant will end up in charge of a shameful son, and will share the family inheritance.
17:3: A pot tests silver and a furnace tests gold, but the LORD tests people's hearts.
17:4: Someone who does wrong listens to lying lips, and a liar pays attention to a wicked tongue.
17:5: Laughing at a poor person insults the God who made them; being glad at someone's disaster will not go unpunished.
17:6: Grandchildren are the crown of the old, and parents are the pride of their children.
17:7: Fine words do not suit a fool — and lying words suit a ruler even less.
17:8: A bribe looks like a magic jewel to whoever gives it; they think it works wherever they turn.
17:9: Covering over a wrong keeps love alive, but bringing it up again and again splits friends apart.
17:10: One word of correction sinks deeper into a wise person than a hundred blows into a fool.
17:11: A bad person only wants to rebel, so a harsh messenger will be sent against him.
17:12: Better to meet a mother bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in the middle of his foolishness.
17:13: If someone pays back good with evil, trouble will never leave their house.
17:14: Starting a quarrel is like letting out water, so drop the matter before the fight breaks out.
17:15: Letting a guilty person off and blaming an innocent one — the LORD hates them both.
17:16: What good is money in a fool's hand to buy wisdom, when he does not really want it?
17:17: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born to help in trouble.
17:18: Only a person with no sense shakes hands to take on a neighbour's debt.
17:19: Whoever loves quarrelling loves doing wrong, and whoever builds his gate too high is asking for ruin.
17:20: A twisted heart finds nothing good, and a lying tongue falls into trouble.
17:21: Having a foolish child brings sorrow; the father of a fool has no joy.
17:22: A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
17:23: A bad person takes a bribe in secret to twist what is fair.
17:24: A person who understands keeps wisdom in view, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
17:25: A foolish son grieves his father and brings bitterness to the mother who bore him.
17:26: It is wrong to punish someone who has done no wrong, or to beat honest leaders for being fair.
17:27: Someone who knows things uses few words, and a person who understands stays calm.
17:28: Even a fool seems wise when he keeps quiet, and sensible when he shuts his mouth.
18:1: Someone who cuts himself off from others only chases what he wants, and argues against all good sense.
18:2: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, only in showing off what he thinks.
18:3: When a bad person arrives, so does scorn; and with shame comes insults.
18:4: The words of a person's mouth are like deep water; the fountain of wisdom is like a flowing stream.
18:5: It is not right to favour a guilty person or to deny justice to an innocent one.
18:6: A fool's lips start fights, and his mouth invites a beating.
18:7: A fool's mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a trap for his own life.
18:8: A gossip's words go down like tasty bites, deep into a person's insides.
18:9: Someone lazy at his work is brother to someone who destroys things.
18:10: The LORD's name is a strong tower; good people run into it and are safe.
18:11: A rich person's money is their strong city; in their mind it is like a high wall.
18:12: Before a crash a person's heart is proud, but humility comes before honour.
18:13: Answering before you have heard the whole story is foolish and shameful.
18:14: A person's spirit can carry them through illness, but if the spirit is crushed, who can bear it?
18:15: A sensible heart gets knowledge, and a wise ear goes looking for it.
18:16: A gift opens doors for a person and brings them before important people.
18:17: Whoever speaks first seems right, until the other person comes and asks questions.
18:18: Drawing lots settles arguments and separates powerful opponents.
18:19: Winning back a brother you have hurt is harder than capturing a strong city; such arguments are like the bars of a fortress.
18:20: What a person says fills their stomach; the words from their lips satisfy them.
18:21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and whoever loves it will eat its fruit.
18:22: Whoever finds a good wife finds something good, and is shown kindness by the LORD.
18:23: A poor person begs politely, but a rich person answers roughly.
18:24: Having too many shallow friends brings ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
19:1: Better to be poor and honest than to be a rich fool who twists his words.
19:2: Being eager without knowing anything is not good, and rushing your feet makes you miss the way.
19:3: A person's own foolishness wrecks their life, and then their heart blames the LORD.
19:4: Money brings many friends, but a poor person's friends leave.
19:5: A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will not get away.
19:6: Many people beg favours from an important person, and everyone is a friend to someone who gives gifts.
19:7: A poor person's own family dislikes him — how much more his friends stay away! He calls after them, but they are gone.
19:8: Whoever gets wisdom loves their own life; whoever holds on to understanding will do well.
19:9: A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will be destroyed.
19:10: Luxury does not suit a fool — and it suits a servant ruling over princes even less.
19:11: Good sense makes a person slow to get angry, and it is to their credit to let a wrong go.
19:12: A king's anger is like a lion roaring, but his kindness is like dew on the grass.
19:13: A foolish son is his father's disaster, and a quarrelling wife is like a tap that keeps dripping.
19:14: A house and money are passed down from parents, but a sensible wife comes from the LORD.
19:15: Being lazy puts a person into a deep sleep, and a slack person goes hungry.
19:16: Keeping the commands keeps your life safe, but ignoring your own way leads to death.
19:17: Being kind to a poor person is like lending to the LORD, and he will pay back the good that was done.
19:18: Correct your child while there is still hope; do not give up on him.
19:19: A hot-tempered person must face the consequences; if you rescue him once, you will have to do it again.
19:20: Listen to advice and take teaching, so that in the end you will be wise.
19:21: People make many plans in their hearts, but it is the LORD's purpose that stands.
19:22: What people want in someone is kindness, and it is better to be poor than to be a liar.
19:23: Respecting the LORD leads to life; you will rest content and not be visited by trouble.
19:24: A lazy person puts his hand in the dish and will not even lift it back to his mouth.
19:25: Punish someone who sneers and the simple will learn caution; correct a person who understands and he will learn even more.
19:26: Whoever mistreats his father and drives away his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
19:27: My son, stop listening to teaching that turns you away from words of knowledge.
19:28: A worthless witness laughs at what is fair, and a bad person's mouth swallows down wrongdoing.
19:29: Punishments are ready for those who sneer, and beatings for the backs of fools.
20:1: Wine makes people mock and strong drink makes them loud; anyone led astray by it is not wise.
20:2: A king's anger is like a lion roaring; making him angry costs you your own life.
20:3: It is an honour to stay out of a fight, but every fool wants to argue.
20:4: A lazy person will not plough because it is cold, so at harvest he looks for a crop and finds nothing.
20:5: The plans in a person's heart are like deep water, but someone who understands can draw them out.
20:6: Plenty of people say how kind they are, but who can find someone you can really trust?
20:7: A good person lives honestly — how happy their children are after them!
20:8: A king sitting on the judgment seat scatters every evil with a look.
20:9: Who can say, "I have kept my heart clean; I am free from wrong"?
20:10: Two different weights and two different measures — the LORD hates them both.
20:11: Even a child shows what they are like by what they do, whether it is pure and right.
20:12: Ears that hear and eyes that see — the LORD made them both.
20:13: Do not love sleep or you will end up poor; keep your eyes open and you will have plenty to eat.
20:14: "No good, no good," says the buyer — then he goes away and boasts about his bargain.
20:15: There is gold and there are many jewels, but lips that speak knowledge are the rarest treasure.
20:16: Take the coat of anyone who promises to pay a stranger's debt; hold it as a pledge.
20:17: Food got by cheating tastes sweet, but afterwards the mouth is full of grit.
20:18: Plans succeed when you talk them over; get good advice before you go to war.
20:19: A gossip gives away secrets, so have nothing to do with someone who talks too much.
20:20: Whoever curses their father or mother will have their lamp go out in pitch darkness.
20:21: Money grabbed quickly at the start will not be a blessing in the end.
20:22: Do not say, "I will pay back the wrong." Wait for the LORD, and he will rescue you.
20:23: The LORD hates two different weights, and scales that cheat are no good either.
20:24: A person's steps are decided by the LORD — so how can anyone fully understand their own way?
20:25: It is a trap to promise something to God without thinking, and only ask questions afterwards.
20:26: A wise king sorts out bad people and runs the threshing wheel over them.
20:27: A person's spirit is the LORD's lamp, searching every corner deep inside them.
20:28: Kindness and honesty keep a king safe, and his throne is held up by kindness.
20:29: Strength is the glory of young people, and grey hair is the honour of the old.
20:30: A beating that hurts can wash away wrong, and blows reach deep inside a person.
21:1: A king's heart is in the LORD's hand, like a channel of water he turns wherever he wants.
21:2: Everything a person does looks right to them, but the LORD weighs the heart.
21:3: Doing what is right and fair pleases the LORD more than offerings do.
21:4: Proud eyes and a proud heart — whatever a bad person produces is sin.
21:5: Careful planning leads to plenty, but rushing leads to going without.
21:6: Getting rich by lying is chasing a puff of smoke and looking for death.
21:7: The violence of bad people will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is fair.
21:8: A guilty person's road is crooked, but someone with a clean heart does what is right.
21:9: Better to live in a corner of the roof than share a big house with someone always quarrelling.
21:10: A bad person wants to do harm, and shows no kindness even to a neighbour.
21:11: When a mocker is punished, simple people learn; when a wise person is taught, he gains knowledge.
21:12: The righteous One watches the house of the wicked and brings bad people down to ruin.
21:13: Whoever shuts their ears to a poor person's cry will call out one day and get no answer.
21:14: A gift given quietly calms anger, and a present slipped into the hand settles rage.
21:15: Doing what is fair brings joy to good people, but terror to those who do wrong.
21:16: Whoever wanders off the road of understanding ends up among the dead.
21:17: Loving a good time makes a person poor; loving wine and rich food never makes anyone rich.
21:18: In the end the bad person pays the price meant for the good, and the cheat for the honest.
21:19: Better to live out in the desert than with a quarrelling, bad-tempered person.
21:20: A wise person's house has treasure and good things stored; a fool swallows up all he gets.
21:21: Whoever chases after doing right and being kind finds life, fairness, and honour.
21:22: A wise person can climb into a city of strong soldiers and pull down the walls they trusted.
21:23: Guarding your mouth and your tongue keeps you out of trouble.
21:24: A proud, big-headed person is called a mocker; everything he does comes out of pride.
21:25: A lazy person's longing will kill him, because his hands refuse to work.
21:26: All day long some people want more and more, but a good person gives and does not hold back.
21:27: The LORD hates what a bad person offers — how much more when it is brought with an evil plan!
21:28: A false witness will be destroyed, but whoever listens carefully will be believed for ever.
21:29: A bad person puts on a bold face, but an honest person thinks about where they are going.
21:30: No wisdom, no understanding, and no plan can stand against the LORD.
21:31: The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but winning belongs to the LORD.
22:1: A good name is worth more than great riches, and being well thought of is better than silver and gold.
22:2: Rich and poor have this in common: the LORD made them both.
22:3: A sensible person sees trouble coming and hides; a simple person walks on and suffers for it.
22:4: Being humble and respecting the LORD brings riches, honour and life.
22:5: Thorns and traps lie on the path of a twisted person, but whoever guards their life stays far away.
22:6: Teach a child the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not leave it.
22:7: The rich rule over the poor, and whoever borrows becomes the lender's servant.
22:8: Whoever plants trouble will harvest disaster, and the stick of their anger will be broken.
22:9: A generous person will be blessed, because they share their food with the poor.
22:10: Send the mocker away and the arguing goes too; quarrels and insults stop.
22:11: Whoever loves a pure heart and speaks kindly will have the king as a friend.
22:12: The LORD's eyes watch over knowledge, but he overturns the words of cheats.
22:13: A lazy person says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the street!"
22:14: The mouth of a woman who is not your wife is a deep pit; anyone the LORD is angry with falls into it.
22:15: Foolishness is tied up in a child's heart, but loving correction drives it far away.
22:16: Squeezing the poor to get rich, or giving presents to the rich, both end in going without.
22:17: Listen carefully to the words of wise people, and set your heart on what I teach,
22:18: because it is good to keep them inside you and have them ready on your lips.
22:19: I am teaching you this today so that you will put your trust in the LORD.
22:20: Have I not written excellent things for you, full of advice and knowledge,
22:21: to show you what is true and certain, so you can give a true answer to whoever sent you?
22:22: Do not rob a poor person just because they are poor, and do not crush someone in need at the city gate,
22:23: because the LORD will take up their case, and will take the life of whoever robbed them.
22:24: Do not make friends with a bad-tempered person or spend time with someone who rages,
22:25: or you will learn their ways and get yourself caught in a trap.
22:26: Do not shake hands on someone else's debt or promise to pay what they owe.
22:27: If you cannot pay, why should the bed be taken from under you?
22:28: Do not move the old boundary stone your ancestors set up.
22:29: Do you see someone who works hard at their job? They will stand before kings, not before nobodies.
23:1: When you sit down to eat with an important person, pay careful attention to what is in front of you.
23:2: If you tend to eat too much, it is like putting a knife to your own throat.
23:3: Do not long for his fine food, because that meal is meant to fool you.
23:4: Do not wear yourself out trying to get rich; be wise enough to stop.
23:5: Why fix your eyes on money that is not even there? It sprouts wings and flies off like an eagle.
23:6: Do not eat the food of a stingy person, or long for his tasty dishes,
23:7: because he is the sort who counts every bite. "Eat! Drink!" he says, but his heart is not with you.
23:8: You will be sick up the little you ate, and all your polite words will be wasted.
23:9: Do not bother speaking to a fool, because he will only look down on your wise words.
23:10: Do not move the old boundary stone or move in on land belonging to children with no father,
23:11: because the one who protects them is strong, and he will take up their case against you.
23:12: Set your heart on being taught, and your ears on words of knowledge.
23:13: Do not leave a child uncorrected; correcting him will not be the end of him.
23:14: Correct him, and you will save his life from the place of the dead.
23:15: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad too.
23:16: I will be delighted deep inside when your lips say what is right.
23:17: Do not let your heart be jealous of people who do wrong; always respect the LORD instead,
23:18: because there is a future for you, and what you hope for will not be cut off.
23:19: Listen, my son, and be wise; keep your heart on the right road.
23:20: Do not spend time with heavy drinkers or people who stuff themselves with meat,
23:21: because drinkers and big eaters end up poor, and sleeping all day leaves a person in rags.
23:22: Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not look down on your mother when she is old.
23:23: Buy the truth and never sell it — and the same with wisdom, teaching and understanding.
23:24: The father of a good child is very glad, and whoever has a wise child is happy in them.
23:25: Make your father and mother glad; give the one who gave you birth a reason to rejoice.
23:26: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
23:27: That kind of woman is a deep pit, a narrow well you cannot climb out of.
23:28: She waits in hiding like a robber, and leads more and more people into doing wrong.
23:29: Who ends up in trouble? Who is sad? Who is fighting? Who is complaining? Who gets hurt for no reason? Whose eyes are red?
23:30: It is the people who sit too long over their wine, always looking for another mixed drink.
23:31: Do not stare at the wine when it glows red and sparkles in the cup and slips down so smoothly — in the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
23:33: Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will say twisted things.
23:34: You will feel like someone lying out at sea, or lying on top of a swaying mast.
23:35: You will say: "They hit me, but I felt nothing. They beat me, but I did not notice. When will I wake up? I want another drink."
24:1: Do not be jealous of bad people, or want to be with them,
24:2: because their hearts plan violence, and their lips talk about causing trouble.
24:3: A house is built with wisdom, and it is made solid with understanding.
24:4: By knowing things, its rooms are filled with all sorts of precious and lovely treasures.
24:5: A wise person is strong, and someone who knows things grows stronger still.
24:6: Go to war with a good plan; with many advisers you will win.
24:7: Wisdom is too high up for a fool to reach, so at the city gate he has nothing to say.
24:8: Whoever plans to do evil will be known as a troublemaker.
24:9: Foolish plans are sin, and everyone hates a mocker.
24:10: If you give up when trouble comes, your strength was small to begin with.
24:11: Rescue those being led away to die; hold back those staggering towards being killed.
24:12: If you say, "But we did not know about this" — does the One who weighs hearts not see it? Does the One who guards your life not know? Will he not pay each person back for what they did?
24:13: My son, eat honey, because it is good; honey from the comb tastes sweet.
24:14: Know that wisdom is just like that for you. Find it, and there is a future for you; what you hope for will not be cut off.
24:15: You bad person, do not lie in wait near a good person's house, or wreck the place where they rest,
24:16: because a good person falls seven times and gets up again, but bad people are knocked flat by trouble.
24:17: Do not be glad when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart cheer when he trips,
24:18: or the LORD will see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
24:19: Do not get upset about people who do evil, and do not be jealous of bad people,
24:20: because there is no future for an evil person; their lamp will be put out.
24:21: My son, respect the LORD and the king, and do not join people who are always after change,
24:22: because disaster will hit them suddenly — and who knows what ruin those two can bring?
24:23: These are also sayings of the wise: showing favour when you judge is not good.
24:24: Whoever tells a guilty person "You are innocent" will be cursed by everyone and hated by every nation,
24:25: but those who correct the guilty will be glad, and rich blessing will come to them.
24:26: Giving an honest answer is like a warm greeting between friends.
24:27: Get your work outside ready and your fields in order — and after that, build your house.
24:28: Do not speak against your neighbour for no reason, or use your mouth to trick people.
24:29: Do not say, "I will do to him what he did to me; I will pay him back for what he did."
24:30: I walked past a lazy person's field and the vineyard of someone with no sense,
24:31: and look — thorns had grown all over it, weeds covered the ground, and the stone wall had fallen down.
24:32: I looked, and I thought hard about it; I looked, and I learned something.
24:33: A little more sleep, a little more dozing, a little more folding your hands to rest —
24:34: and being poor will come at you like a robber, and going without like an armed man.
25:1: These are more of Solomon's wise sayings, copied out by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
25:2: It is God's glory to keep a matter hidden, and a king's glory to search a matter out.
25:3: The sky is high, the earth is deep, and a king's heart cannot be worked out either.
25:4: Take the waste out of the silver, and the silversmith can make a beautiful dish.
25:5: Take bad people away from the king, and his throne will stand firm on doing right.
25:6: Do not push yourself forward in front of the king, or stand in the place meant for important people.
25:7: It is better to be told "Come up here" than to be moved down in front of a prince you can see.
25:8: Do not rush off to start an argument, or you may not know what to do when your neighbour shames you in the end.
25:9: If you have a disagreement, settle it with that person alone, and do not give away someone else's secret,
25:10: or whoever hears it will shame you, and your bad name will stick.
25:11: A word spoken at just the right time is like golden apples in a silver setting.
25:12: A wise correction to a listening ear is like a gold earring or fine gold jewellery.
25:13: A trustworthy messenger refreshes whoever sent him, like the coolness of snow at harvest time.
25:14: Someone who boasts about gifts they never give is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
25:15: Patience can win over a ruler, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
25:16: Have you found honey? Eat just enough — too much and you will be sick.
25:17: Do not go to your neighbour's house too often, or he will get tired of you and start to dislike you.
25:18: Telling lies about your neighbour is like a heavy hammer, a sword, and a sharp arrow.
25:19: Trusting an unreliable person in trouble is like a broken tooth or a foot that gives way.
25:20: Singing cheerful songs to a sad heart is like taking someone's coat away in cold weather, or pouring vinegar on soda.
25:21: If your enemy is hungry, give him food; if he is thirsty, give him water,
25:22: because doing that heaps burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
25:23: The north wind brings rain, and a gossiping tongue brings angry faces.
25:24: Better to live in a corner of the roof than share a big house with someone always quarrelling.
25:25: Good news from a faraway country is like cold water to someone very thirsty.
25:26: A good person who gives way to a bad one is like a muddied spring or a spoiled well.
25:27: Eating too much honey is not good, and neither is chasing after your own glory.
25:28: Someone who cannot control their own temper is like a city with its walls broken down.
26:1: Snow in summer and rain at harvest are both out of place — and so is honour given to a fool.
26:2: Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, a curse with no reason behind it never lands.
26:3: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a stick for the back of a fool.
26:4: Do not answer a fool with his own foolishness, or you will end up just like him.
26:5: Answer a fool with his own foolishness, or he will think he is wise.
26:6: Sending a message by a fool is like cutting off your own feet and asking for trouble.
26:7: A wise saying in a fool's mouth is as useless as the legs of someone who cannot walk.
26:8: Giving honour to a fool is like tying a stone into a sling.
26:9: A wise saying in a fool's mouth is like a thorn stuck in a drunk person's hand.
26:10: Hiring a fool or a passer-by is like an archer firing arrows at everyone.
26:11: A fool goes back to his foolishness again and again, like a dog going back to its vomit.
26:12: Do you see someone who thinks he is wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
26:13: A lazy person says, "There is a fierce lion on the road! A lion in the streets!"
26:14: A door turns on its hinges, and a lazy person turns over in bed.
26:15: A lazy person puts his hand in the dish and finds it too much trouble to lift it back to his mouth.
26:16: A lazy person thinks he is wiser than seven people who can give a sensible answer.
26:17: Jumping into someone else's quarrel as you pass by is like grabbing a dog by the ears.
26:18: Someone who tricks their neighbour and then says "I was only joking!" is like a madman throwing firebrands, arrows and death about.
26:20: Without wood a fire goes out, and without a gossip a quarrel dies down.
26:21: As coals feed hot coals and wood feeds fire, so a quarrelsome person keeps a fight burning.
26:22: A gossip's words go down like tasty bites, deep into a person's insides.
26:23: Warm words from a wicked heart are like a cheap clay pot coated with silver waste.
26:24: Someone who hates you covers it up with their words while hiding tricks inside,
26:25: so when they speak sweetly do not believe them, because their heart is full of wickedness.
26:26: Their hatred may be hidden behind tricks, but their wickedness will be shown to everyone.
26:27: Whoever digs a pit falls into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have it roll back on them.
26:28: A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and smooth talk ruins others.
27:1: Do not boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what a single day will bring.
27:2: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth; a stranger, not your own lips.
27:3: A stone is heavy and sand is a weight, but a fool's anger is heavier than both.
27:4: Anger is cruel and rage is a flood, but who can stand up against jealousy?
27:5: Being corrected openly is better than being loved in secret.
27:6: A friend who hurts you means well; an enemy's many kisses do not.
27:7: A full person turns down honey, but to a hungry person even bitter food tastes sweet.
27:8: Someone far from home is like a bird that has wandered from its nest.
27:9: Sweet oil and perfume make the heart glad, and so does a friend's honest advice.
27:10: Do not leave your own friend or your father's friend. When trouble comes, do not go to a distant relative — a neighbour nearby is better than a brother far away.
27:11: My son, be wise and make my heart glad, so I can answer anyone who mocks me.
27:12: A sensible person sees trouble coming and hides; a simple person walks on and suffers for it.
27:13: Take the coat of anyone who promises to pay a stranger's debt; hold it as a pledge.
27:14: Shouting a loud blessing to your neighbour early in the morning will be taken as a curse.
27:15: A quarrelsome person is like a tap dripping all through a rainy day.
27:16: Trying to hold them back is like holding back the wind, or grabbing oil with your hand.
27:17: Iron sharpens iron, and one person sharpens another.
27:18: Whoever looks after the fig tree gets to eat its fruit, and whoever looks after their master is honoured.
27:19: Water reflects a face, and a person's heart reflects the person.
27:20: Death and the grave are never full, and neither are human eyes.
27:21: A pot tests silver and a furnace tests gold, and praise tests a person.
27:22: You could crush a fool with grain in a bowl, and his foolishness still would not leave him.
27:23: Know exactly how your flocks are doing, and take good care of your herds,
27:24: because riches do not last for ever, and a crown does not pass down through every generation.
27:25: The hay is cut, new grass appears, and the mountain plants are gathered in.
27:26: The lambs will give you clothing, and the goats will pay for a field.
27:27: There will be plenty of goats' milk for your food, for your household, and for your servant girls.
28:1: Bad people run away when nobody is chasing them, but good people are as bold as a lion.
28:2: When a country does wrong, its rulers keep changing; but with a wise, understanding leader it stays steady.
28:3: A poor person who bullies the poor is like a downpour that washes away the crop.
28:4: Those who turn away from the law praise bad people, but those who keep it stand against them.
28:5: Bad people do not understand what is fair, but those who look for the LORD understand everything.
28:6: Better to be poor and honest than rich and crooked.
28:7: Keeping the law makes a wise son, but keeping company with greedy people shames his father.
28:8: Whoever grows rich by charging too much is saving it up for someone who is kind to the poor.
28:9: If someone turns their ear away from the law, even their prayers are hateful.
28:10: Whoever leads honest people down a bad road falls into their own pit, but the whole-hearted inherit good things.
28:11: A rich person thinks he is wise, but a poor person who understands sees right through him.
28:12: When good people succeed there is great glory, but when bad people rise everyone hides.
28:13: Covering up your wrongs will not go well, but owning up and turning away from them brings mercy.
28:14: Happy is the person who is always careful, but a stubborn heart falls into trouble.
28:15: A cruel ruler over poor people is like a roaring lion or a prowling bear.
28:16: A ruler without understanding bullies people, but whoever hates dishonest gain will live long.
28:17: Someone weighed down by having shed blood will run to the pit; let nobody stop him.
28:18: Whoever lives honestly will be kept safe, but whoever lives crookedly will fall all at once.
28:19: Whoever works their own field will have plenty of food, but chasing empty things brings plenty of poverty.
28:20: A trustworthy person will be richly blessed, but whoever rushes to get rich will not go unpunished.
28:21: Showing favour is not good — some people will do wrong for a single piece of bread.
28:22: A stingy person rushes after money and does not realise that poverty is coming for them.
28:23: In the end people are more grateful to someone who corrected them than to someone who flattered them.
28:24: Whoever robs their father or mother and says "That is not wrong" is no different from a destroyer.
28:25: A greedy heart starts fights, but whoever trusts the LORD will do well.
28:26: Trusting only your own heart is foolish, but whoever walks wisely will be kept safe.
28:27: Whoever gives to the poor will not go without, but whoever looks the other way gets many curses.
28:28: When bad people rise, everyone hides; when they fall, good people flourish.
29:1: Someone corrected again and again who still stiffens his neck will be broken suddenly, past mending.
29:2: When good people are in charge, the people are glad; when bad people rule, the people groan.
29:3: Whoever loves wisdom makes his father glad, but keeping bad company wastes his money.
29:4: A king makes a country steady by being fair, but demanding bribes tears it down.
29:5: Flattering your neighbour is spreading a net in front of their feet.
29:6: Bad people are trapped by their own wrongdoing, but good people sing and are glad.
29:7: A good person cares about justice for the poor, but a bad person does not even want to know.
29:8: Mockers set a whole city alight, but wise people calm anger down.
29:9: When a wise person argues with a fool, the fool rages or laughs and there is no peace.
29:10: Violent people hate an honest person, but the upright care about his life.
29:11: A fool lets out everything he feels, but a wise person holds it back.
29:12: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials turn out wicked.
29:13: A poor person and an oppressor have this in common: the LORD gives light to both their eyes.
29:14: If a king judges the poor honestly, his throne will stand firm for ever.
29:15: Correction gives wisdom, but a child left to himself shames his mother.
29:16: When bad people increase, so does wrongdoing, but good people will see them fall.
29:17: Correct your child and he will give you peace; he will bring joy to your heart.
29:18: Where nobody sees what God is showing, people run wild — but whoever keeps the law is happy.
29:19: A servant will not be corrected by words alone; he may understand and still not act.
29:20: Do you see someone who speaks without thinking? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
29:21: Spoil a servant from childhood, and in the end he will act as if he owns the place.
29:22: A hot-tempered person starts quarrels, and an angry one does plenty of wrong.
29:23: Pride brings a person low, but a humble spirit gains honour.
29:24: Sharing with a thief means hating your own life; you hear the oath and say nothing.
29:25: Being afraid of people is a trap, but whoever trusts the LORD is safe.
29:26: Many people want the ruler's favour, but it is the LORD who decides what is fair.
29:27: Good people cannot stand what is unfair, and bad people cannot stand someone honest.
30:1: The words of Agur son of Jakeh — what he said to Ithiel and to Ucal:
30:2: I am more stupid than anyone else; I do not have the understanding a person should have.
30:3: I never learned wisdom, and I do not know the Holy One.
30:4: Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloak? Who set the ends of the earth in place? What is his name, and his son's name? Do you know?
30:5: Every word of God is pure; he is a shield to everyone who trusts him.
30:6: Do not add to his words, or he will correct you and you will be shown up as a liar.
30:7: I ask you for two things; do not say no to me before I die:
30:8: Keep lying and cheating far from me. Do not make me poor or rich; just give me the food I need,
30:9: or I might be full and say, "Who is the LORD?" — or be poor and steal, and shame God's name.
30:10: Do not tell tales about a servant to his master, or he will curse you and you will be in the wrong.
30:11: There are people who curse their fathers and never bless their mothers.
30:12: There are people who think they are clean, but have never washed off their dirt.
30:13: There are people whose eyes are so proud, whose eyelids are lifted so high.
30:14: There are people whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, eating up the poor and needy of the earth.
30:15: The leech has two daughters who cry, "Give! Give!" There are three things never satisfied, four that never say "enough":
30:16: the grave, a womb with no child, land that never gets enough water, and fire.
30:17: The eye that laughs at a father and refuses to obey a mother will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by young eagles.
30:18: There are three things too wonderful for me, four I cannot work out:
30:19: the way an eagle flies in the sky, the way a snake moves over a rock, the way a ship sails the sea, and the way a man is with a young woman.
30:20: This is the way of a woman who breaks her marriage: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
30:21: Three things make the earth shake, four it cannot put up with:
30:22: a servant who becomes king, a fool who has eaten his fill,
30:23: a hateful woman who gets married, and a servant girl who takes her mistress's place.
30:24: There are four things on earth that are small, but very wise:
30:25: ants are not strong, yet they store up their food in summer;
30:26: rock badgers are not powerful, yet they make their homes in the cliffs;
30:27: locusts have no king, yet they all march out in ranks;
30:28: a lizard can be caught in your hand, yet it lives in kings' palaces.
30:29: There are three things that walk proudly, four that move beautifully:
30:30: a lion, strongest of the animals, that turns back from nothing;
30:31: a strutting rooster, a male goat, and a king with his army around him.
30:32: If you have been foolish and full of yourself, or planned something bad, put your hand over your mouth,
30:33: because churning milk makes butter, twisting a nose makes it bleed, and stirring up anger makes a fight.
31:1: The words of King Lemuel — the message his mother taught him:
31:2: My son! Son that I gave birth to! Son that I promised to God! What shall I teach you?
31:3: Do not give your strength away to women, or your ways to what ruins kings.
31:4: Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, and not for rulers to crave strong drink,
31:5: or they will drink and forget the law, and take away what is fair from people who are suffering.
31:6: Give strong drink to someone who is dying, and wine to someone whose heart is heavy.
31:7: Let them drink and forget how poor they are, and remember their misery no more.
31:8: Speak up for people who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of everyone left with nothing.
31:9: Speak up and judge fairly; defend the poor and the needy.
31:10: Who can find a capable wife? She is worth far more than jewels.
31:11: Her husband trusts her completely, and he lacks nothing of value.
31:12: She does him good and never harm, all the days of her life.
31:13: She looks for wool and flax and works gladly with her hands.
31:14: She is like trading ships, bringing food from far away.
31:15: She gets up while it is still dark to give her household food and to set the servant girls their work.
31:16: She looks at a field and buys it; with what she has earned she plants a vineyard.
31:17: She rolls up her sleeves and makes her arms strong.
31:18: She knows her work is worth doing, and her lamp does not go out at night.
31:19: Her hands hold the spinning stick and the spindle.
31:20: She opens her hand to the poor and reaches out to help those in need.
31:21: She is not worried about snow for her household, because they are all warmly dressed in red.
31:22: She makes her own bed coverings; her clothes are fine linen and purple.
31:23: Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he sits with the town elders.
31:24: She makes fine linen clothes and sells them, and supplies belts to the traders.
31:25: Strength and dignity are what she wears, and she can laugh at whatever is coming.
31:26: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and kind teaching is on her tongue.
31:27: She watches over her household and never eats the bread of laziness.
31:28: Her children stand up and call her happy, and her husband praises her too:
31:29: "Many women do capable things, but you are better than them all."
31:30: Charm can fool you and beauty does not last, but a woman who respects the LORD deserves the praise.
31:31: Give her the reward she has earned, and let what she has done be praised at the city gate.
